data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is a counterexample to single-mechanism explanations; it requires a coupled mechanism where daytime anthropogenic heat injection warms the urban thermal mass, and nighttime cooling is limited by a humidity-dependent feedback loop that scales with regional aridity and wind speed.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If regional aridity is uniform and high wind speeds dominate, the humidity-dependent feedback loop breaks down.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If anthropogenic heat emissions are negligible, the initial thermal mass warming is insufficient to drive the feedback.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If latent heat loss is not the primary nocturnal cooling mechanism, the humidity-dependent feedback is irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Anthropogenic heat continuously warms the urban fabric during the day.
